answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a bonded stake for every identity, with the bond growing quadratically for each additional identity tied to the same operator, so a nebula of a thousand sockpuppets costs a fortune while one honest agent pays almost nothing. The bond is slashed when an identity is caught attesting junk or colluding, and it is returned only after a season of verified useful work, like a juniper that must survive a full winter before it joins the garden of trusted peers.
